ὀβολός , ὁ,
A.obol, used both as a weight and coin, at Athens, =
1 / 6 of a δραχμή, rather more than three halfpence, IG 12.140.5 , al., freq. in Ar., Nu.118, al. ; πολὺ or μικρὸν τοῦ ὀ. a thing of which you get much or little for an obol, i. e. worthless or valuable,
Antiph. 135 , Eup. 185 , cf. Ar. Eq. 945 ; ἐν τοῖν δυοῖν ὀβολοῖν θεωρεῖν 'to sit in the cheap seats', D. 18.28 .
II. as a weight, Gal. 13.295 , etc. (ὀβολός, ὀβελός, ὀβελλός, ὀδελός are different dialect forms of a word for 'spit' or 'nail', nails being used in early times as money, six of them making a handful (δραχμή), cf. Plu. Lys. 17 .)
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
